sections.description: Laws concerning the various types of offerings

sections.description: Consecration of Aaron and his sons; death of Nadab and Abihu

sections.title: The Holiness Code
sections.description: Laws concerning holiness, festivals, the sabbatical year, and the blessings and curses of the covenant

events.title: The Laws of Sacrifice Are Given
events.description: The Lord speaks to Moses from the tent of meeting and gives him detailed laws about the five main offerings: the burnt offering, the grain offering, the peace offering, the sin offering, and the guilt offering. These laws are to govern Israel's worship at the tabernacle.

events.title: Aaron and his sons are consecrated as priests
events.description: Moses performs the consecration ceremony for Aaron and his four sons as priests, just as the Lord commanded. They are washed, clothed in holy priestly garments, and anointed with oil. The consecration lasts seven days, during which they must remain in the tent of meeting at all times.

events.title: The Priests' First Service
events.description: On the eighth day, Aaron begins his priestly service. He offers a sin offering and a burnt offering for himself and for the people. The glory of the Lord appears to the entire congregation, and fire from the Lord consumes the sacrifice on the altar. The people shout for joy and fall face down.

events.title: The Death of Nadab and Abihu
events.description: Aaron's sons Nadab and Abihu offer unauthorized fire before the Lord, which He had not commanded them. Fire comes out from the Lord and consumes them, and they die in the presence of the Lord. Moses forbids Aaron and his remaining sons from mourning openly.

events.title: Rules for Mourning and Holy Conduct
events.description: After the tragedy involving Nadab and Abihu, God gives new rules for the priests. The priests must not drink wine when serving in the tabernacle. They are to distinguish between holy and common, between clean and unclean, and teach the Israelites all the laws the Lord has given.

events.title: Clean and Unclean Animals
events.description: God gives Moses and Aaron detailed rules about which animals the Israelites may and may not eat. Land animals must have split hooves and chew the cud. Fish must have fins and scales. Specific birds, reptiles, and insects are considered unclean.

events.title: Purification After Childbirth
events.description: God gives laws concerning a woman's uncleanness after childbirth. After giving birth to a son, she is unclean for seven days; after giving birth to a daughter, for fourteen days. At the end of her purification period, she must offer a burnt offering and a sin offering.

events.title: Laws Concerning Leprosy
events.description: God gives detailed rules for how priests should examine and judge skin diseases and leprosy. The infected person must live outside the camp and cry out, "Unclean! Unclean!". The laws also cover the purification ritual when someone is healed, involving an offering of two birds, cedar wood, scarlet yarn, and hyssop.

events.title: The Day of Atonement Established
events.description: God establishes Yom Kippur, the great Day of Atonement, as the most important day in Israel's religious calendar. Once a year, the high priest must enter the Most Holy Place with blood to make atonement for all the people's sins. Two goats are chosen: one is sacrificed as a sin offering, and after Aaron lays the people's sins upon it, the scapegoat is sent away into the wilderness.

events.title: Prohibition Against Eating Blood
events.description: God forbids the Israelites to eat blood of any kind. The blood is the life of the animal, and God has given it for use on the altar to make atonement. Anyone who eats blood shall be cut off from the people.

events.title: "Be holy, for I am holy"
events.description: God gives the holiness law with the central command: "Love your neighbor as yourself." The chapter contains various ethical laws concerning justice, care for the poor and foreigners, honesty in business, and respect for the elderly. Everything is founded on God's own holiness.

events.title: The Lord's Feasts
events.description: God establishes the major feasts in Israel's calendar: the Sabbath, Passover and the Feast of Unleavened Bread, the Day of Firstfruits, the Feast of Weeks (Pentecost), the Feast of Trumpets, the Day of Atonement, and the Feast of Tabernacles. These feasts are to be holy assemblies for all generations.

events.title: The Blasphemer Stoned
events.description: A man with an Israelite mother and an Egyptian father gets into a quarrel in the camp and blasphemes God's name. He is brought to Moses, and the Lord commands that the whole congregation stone him. God also gives the law that anyone who blasphemes the Lord's name shall die.

events.title: The Sabbath Year and the Jubilee
events.description: God institutes the Sabbath year: every seventh year the land must rest and lie fallow. After seven Sabbath years, in the fiftieth year, the Jubilee is to be celebrated. All land shall then return to its original owner, all Israelite slaves are to be freed, and debts are to be forgiven. The trumpet shall sound throughout the land.

events.title: Blessings and Curses
events.description: God concludes the holiness law with promises of blessing for obedience and warnings of curses for disobedience. The blessings include good harvests, peace, and God's presence. The curses include disease, war, famine, and exile. Nevertheless, God promises that he will not utterly reject them but will remember the covenant with their ancestors.
